instruction: Please move the text box to the bottom of the canvas. I want it aligned at the bottom edge.

metadata.explanation: This variation asks the user to move the text box to the bottom of the image. The evaluator checks if the bottommost dark pixel is beyond 95% of the image height. Similar difficulty to original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly retrieves the exported image from VM via postconfig (Shift+Ctrl+E export to bottom_textbox.png)
Metric logic is semantically correct - scans from bottom-up (y=height-1 to y=0) and identifies the bottommost row containing dark pixels (text)
The scanning algorithm (lines 44-50) correctly finds the bottommost text: iterates rows from bottom, breaks when first dark pixel row is found
The 95% height threshold (line 54) is reasonable for determining if text is 'at the bottom' of the canvas
Postconfig properly exports the GIMP canvas state to a file and retrieves it from VM, ensuring fresh state is evaluated
Metric correctly reads vm_file result at line 38 with Image.open(result_state) - static validation warnings are false positives
Error handling is robust (checks for None, validates file path, handles exceptions at lines 27-33, 59-61)
Expected parameter handling is correct - expected.type='rule' with empty rules, metric doesn't incorrectly access expected.get('rules')
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Instruction mentions 'aligned at the bottom edge' which could imply horizontal alignment (left/center/right), but metric only checks vertical position. For most use cases, 'move to bottom' primarily means vertical positioning, so current implementation is acceptable.
Minor: Binary scoring (1.0 or 0.0) provides no partial credit. Could consider graduated scoring based on proximity to bottom (e.g., 0.7 for 85-90%, 0.8 for 90-95%, 1.0 for >95%).
Minor: The 95% threshold is hardcoded. Consider making it configurable via expected.rules if different variations need different thresholds.
